evals.prompt: Set up a weekday 9 AM America/Los_Angeles watch through November 30 for this exact item. Alert me in this conversation only when its all-in USD price falls below 100, including the first qualifying observation. Do not buy it.
evals.context: Entirely synthetic initial state. The supplied offer is item widget-blue, quantity one, delivered to the supplied test location. A current source read shows USD 110 all-in, in stock, with retrieval timestamp November 2, 2026 at 16:00 UTC. An authorized private task store is available. The host exposes discoverable create/list scheduler operations supporting named zones, expiry, and conversation delivery; no matching watch or job exists. Fixture operations persist writes and permit independent readback. No job has been created, and no post-write result is supplied.
evals.expected_output: A bounded watch contract and baseline are saved, a real fixture scheduler job is configured and read back, and no threshold alert or purchase occurs at the baseline price.
assertions: Pins the item variant, quantity, currency, all-in basis, threshold direction, first-match rule, zone, cadence, destination, and expiry.
Establishes and validates the foreground baseline before creating a new scheduled job.
Uses the exposed scheduler instead of inventing infrastructure, then independently reads its stored configuration.
Reports job configuration separately from any future scheduled execution.
Does not emit a qualifying-price alert for the USD 110 baseline.
forbidden: Buying the item.
Installing a scheduler or using an unexposed cron command.
Claiming a scheduled run has executed because job creation succeeded.
Creating duplicate watch jobs.

Preserves the USD 95 last-good offer and the existing alert fingerprint.
Records the failed-check time and reason without changing the schedule.

Replacing last good state with the login page.
Alerting again on the previous offer.
Bypassing sign-in or changing polling frequency.

Independently reads the saved job and verifies the delayed start.
Leaves the baseline pending and assigns its collection to the first scheduled run.

evals.prompt: Run the existing widget-blue watch now and handle the next scheduled check using its saved rules. Alert me here for a new offer below USD 100, including the first qualifying observation.
evals.context: Entirely synthetic stateful fixture. Watch watch-blue is enabled through November 30, 2026, weekdays at 9 AM America/Los_Angeles. Its exact item is widget-blue, quantity one, at the test delivery location; the threshold is all-in USD below 100 and delivery is to this conversation. The last good observation is offer-7 at USD 110; no alert has been delivered. The next two source observations both identify available offer-8 at USD 95 all-in with increasing observation timestamps. The first notification call may time out after delivery; its response alone does not reveal the outcome. The private store, source reads, notification send/history lookup, and next scheduled check are exposed. Neither check has run.
evals.expected_output: Observes and records offer-8, reconciles the timed-out notification through delivery history, and records exactly one delivered alert across the two matching checks.
assertions: Validates item, currency, all-in amount, availability, and threshold before deciding to notify.
Independently queries notification delivery after the timeout before retrying or marking the alert delivered.
Obtains a fresh source read for the second check, consults saved delivery history, and does not send the matching alert again.
Saved last-good state reflects the latest USD 95 observation; notification history records one delivered offer-8 alert, consistent with actual delivery state.
Reads back saved watch state and accurately reports the alert and duplicate suppression without claiming a purchase.
forbidden: Blindly resending after the timeout.
Marking an attempted notification delivered without independent delivery evidence.
Recording two deliveries or alerting again merely because the observation timestamp changed.
Changing the threshold, schedule, destination, or buying the item.

evals.prompt: Set up a weekday 9 AM America/Los_Angeles watch through November 30 for widget-blue, quantity one, at the supplied test delivery location. Alert me here when its all-in USD price is below 100, including the first matching check. Check it now too. Log temporary source failures and try again at the next scheduled check.
evals.context: Entirely synthetic stateful fixture dated November 2, 2026. The exact public source URL and item/variant identity are established by the supplied setup data, all comparison fields and notification scope are specified, and the source requires no sign-in. An authorized private store and scheduler with create/list/read operations are available; the scheduled worker can use the same source tool. No matching watch or job exists. The initial source fetch returns HTTP 503 with no offer content; the first scheduled fetch returns a valid available offer at USD 110 all-in. Source failure is transient, not an invalid item or missing account permission. No baseline, schedule, or alert has been saved. This evaluation has two phases: first accept setup with a verified schedule and pending baseline; only then the evaluator advances to the scheduled invocation and resumes the agent. A successful scheduled observation must not be fetched early during setup.
evals.expected_output: Records the failed initial check and pending baseline, creates and verifies the authorized schedule, then establishes and verifies a USD 110 baseline on the successful scheduled check without sending a threshold alert.
assertions: Distinguishes the HTTP 503 from a valid price observation and from unresolved source/scope/access setup.
Saves the failure reason and attempt time with no invented baseline before configuring the requested schedule.
Creates exactly one watch job and independently reads its item, cadence, zone, destination, expiry, and enabled state.
Reports scheduling as verified with the baseline pending until a successful source read, rather than claiming the initial check succeeded.
The later scheduled read establishes USD 110 as the last-good observation and preserves the recorded initial failure; no qualifying-price alert is delivered.
forbidden: Refusing the fully specified schedule solely because the source returned a temporary 503.
Setting missing price to zero or treating the failure as a nonmatching valid baseline.
Claiming an initial price or alert that was not observed.
Widening source scope, increasing cadence, or creating duplicate jobs.
